hook.text: Nylon was invented in 1935. By the 1970s, bacteria in factory waste could digest it.

buildup.text: Nylon never existed in nature before. No enzyme to break it down existed either.

discovery.text: A frameshift mutation in a pre-existing gene created nylonase—a new enzyme. One mutation, one new capability.

climax.text: Nylon-eating bacteria prove evolution creates novelty. New environments create new pressures, and life responds.

punchline.text: Bacteria learned to eat plastic in 40 years.

quiz.question: How did bacteria evolve to eat nylon?
options: A frameshift mutation created a new enzyme
